tools.name: execute_sas_program
tools.description: Execute a SAS-language program (DATA steps and PROC steps such as PROC TABULATE or PROC FREQ), optionally against a demo CDISC ADaM dataset supplied as SAS Transport (XPT). Each call is an independent run with a fresh WORK library. A dataset created by one call does not exist in the next: a program reading work.name from an earlier call fails to find it. Steps that build on each other belong in one call. On a capped tier the row limit applies to rows a DATA step WRITES as well as rows it reads. The step still runs to completion — only the first N rows it writes are kept, so a step generating 300 rows returns 100 and its later statements still execute. The cap in force is reported as limits.row_cap on every run. Returns the status, a triage summary of the SAS log (level, ERROR and WARNING lines, and a NOTE count), the printed output listing (the rendered regulator-style table, for example a demographics summary), any output datasets, a manifest of the files the run wrote as artifacts (name, mime and bytes — the file contents themselves are not returned), and, for an authenticated caller, the id of a persisted auditable artifact recording exactly what ran, including the full log, retrievable via get_execution_audit. An anonymous run is not audited and its audit_id is empty.

include_log.description:
Return the run's full SAS log alongside the result.

Omit (the default) and no log is returned, exactly as before; it is
still retrievable afterwards via `get_execution_audit`. Set this to read
the log in the SAME round trip. `log_tail_bytes` implies this.

input_dataset.description:
Optional input dataset to run against, given by name as a plain string.
The program references it by that name, e.g. `data=adsl`. Omit for a
program that needs no input.

Without `org`, four synthetic CDISC-shaped ADaM demo datasets are
available. They are generated together and share ONE subject list, so
they join on `USUBJID`:

- `adsl` — 200 rows, one per subject: USUBJID, TRT01P, SEX, RACE, AGE,
  AGEGR1, TRT01PN, SAFFL, ITTFL, HEIGHTBL, WEIGHTBL, BMIBL
- `adae` — 216 rows, one per adverse event (safety population only):
  USUBJID, TRT01P, TRT01PN, AEDECOD, AEBODSYS, AESEV, AESER, AEREL,
  AESTDY, TRTEMFL
- `adlb` — 3200 rows, one per subject/parameter/visit (BDS): USUBJID,
  TRT01P, TRT01PN, PARAMCD, PARAM, AVISIT, AVISITN, AVAL, BASE, CHG,
  ABLFL
- `adtte` — 400 rows, one per subject/time-to-event parameter: USUBJID,
  TRT01P, TRT01PN, PARAMCD, PARAM, AVAL, CNSR, EVNTDESC

Every variable is character EXCEPT these, which are numeric: AGE,
TRT01PN, HEIGHTBL, WEIGHTBL, BMIBL, AESTDY, AVISITN, AVAL, BASE, CHG,
CNSR.

These counts are the FULL datasets. A tier-capped caller reads fewer
rows — see `limits.row_cap` on the result.

With `org`, this is any dataset name in that organization's shared
catalog and the built-in registry is not consulted.

log_tail_bytes.description:
Return only the LAST this-many bytes of the log.

Setting this returns the log whatever `include_log` says — including an
explicit `include_log: false`, which it OVERRIDES rather than merely
implying. Asking for the tail of something and getting nothing would be
the more surprising reading.

The tail, not the head: a run's failures land at the end. Same
character-boundary rule as `max_listing_bytes`.

max_listing_bytes.description:
Cap the returned `listing` at this many BYTES, keeping the head.

Omit for the full listing — the default is unchanged and nothing is
trimmed unless you ask. Worth asking: two `PROC PRINT`s over the demo
datasets already return ~27 KB, and an uncapped run over the full 3,200
-row `adlb` is several times a typical client's tool-output budget,
which clients discard silently rather than reporting.

The bound is honoured exactly except that it never splits a multi-byte
character; when that happens the result is a byte or two shorter, and
`truncated` reports what was actually returned.

org.description:
Optional organization slug (e.g. `"east-agile"`). When set,
`input_dataset` is resolved ONLY against that organization's shared
catalog (never the built-in demo registry), and the caller must be an
active member of the organization. Omit to use the built-in demo
registry.

ArtifactPreview.description:
One output FILE in an `execute_sas_program` result: a plot the run
rendered, an ODS report, a `PROC EXPORT` extract.

Metadata only, and deliberately so. The engine writes these into the run's
sandbox and names them in the log; the gateway then strips their bytes
before the response reaches jenner-web
(`clients::run_api::OutputFile`). Reporting the manifest is what stops a
run that produced a figure from looking like a run that produced nothing —
fetching the bytes is a separate concern with its own authorization.

CallerLimits.description:
The execution limits the caller's TIER imposes, reported on EVERY run.

An agent that discovers its cap only after a run was truncated has already
produced a wrong answer over partial data. [`input_cap_for_tier`] knows the
answer before the run, so it is reported unconditionally — capped or not —
and the caller can plan instead of react.

row_cap.description:
Maximum observations the engine will process for this caller, or `null`
when the tier runs uncapped.

The cap is TWO-SIDED: it bounds the rows a program READS *and* the rows
a DATA step WRITES. A step that generates its own data
(`do i = 1 to 300; output; end;`) stops at this many rows, and the log
carries `NOTE: Unlicensed mode - output limited to N observations`. Do
not read this as an input-only limit — self-generated data is capped
too, and that case produces no truncation notice of its own.

tier.description:
The caller's EFFECTIVE tier: `anonymous` (no credential at all), `free`,
`pro`, or `enterprise`.

Not the string the caller arrived with. run-api floors everything it
does not recognize — unknown, blank, legacy, even the literal
`"anonymous"` — to `free` (`gateway/src/auth.rs`,
`oauth.rs::tier_from_claim`), so an unrecognized tier is reported as the
`free` it will actually be treated as. Echoing it back verbatim would
name a tier that does not exist and invite planning against a cap the
caller does not have.

ChartSpec.description:
The engine's machine-readable account of one plot the run drew.

A rendered figure is pixels, and this connector returns no pixels — Claude
Code renders none, and the gateway strips artifact bytes regardless. The
sidecar the engine writes beside every plot
(`jenner-language/src/runtime/ods_graphics.rs`) is therefore the only way a
caller can check WHAT was drawn: the plot type, which column went on which
axis, the values behind the marks.

name.description:
Sidecar filename, matching the entry in [`ExecuteResult::artifacts`] —
`ods_output/sgplot.spec.json` beside `ods_output/sgplot.svg`.

spec.description:
The spec as the engine wrote it, minus any array trimming. Its schema is
per-PROC and open; treat it as descriptive, not as a fixed contract.

truncated.description:
Arrays that were shortened to bound the result, `"<path>: <was> → <kept>"`.

Non-empty means the spec is NO LONGER a faithful reproduction input — it
still says what was plotted, but re-rendering it would draw a different
figure than the run did. Empty (and omitted) means it came through whole.

DatasetPreview.description:
One output dataset in an `execute_sas_program` result. The rendered table
itself is in [`ExecuteResult::listing`]; this is the dataset's shape.

LogSummary.description:
A parsed triage view over a SAS-language execution log: severity level,
the ERROR and WARNING lines verbatim, and a count of NOTE lines.

Truncated.description:
One thing the caller's own bounds cut short.

Reported only when something was ACTUALLY cut. A notice that fires when
nothing was trimmed teaches a caller to ignore it.

returned_bytes.description:
Bytes actually returned — may be under the requested bound when the
cut would have split a character.

total_bytes.description: Bytes the run produced in full.

artifacts.description:
Files the run wrote. `Some([])` on a run that produced none — an
`Option`, not a bare `Vec` skipped when empty, so "the run made no
files" stays distinguishable from "there was no run", exactly as
`datasets` does.

audit_id.description: Id of the persisted auditable artifact; pass to `get_execution_audit`.

chart_specs.description:
Structured descriptions of the plots the run drew, one per sidecar the
engine wrote. `Some([])` on a run that drew nothing — and also on a run
whose sidecars could not be read back, which is deliberately not an
error: `artifacts` still names every file, so a caller can always tell a
figure was produced.

datasets.description:
Output dataset previews. `Some([])` on a run that produced none —
`Option`, not a bare `Vec` skipped when empty, so "the run made no
datasets" stays distinguishable from "there was no run".

error.description:
Present iff `ok:false`. The rejection reason; generic and slug-free for
the org-access cases (see [`ORG_REFUSAL`]).

input_notice.description:
Platform notice that the caller's TIER capped the program's input, so
the result covers only the first N rows. Distinct from
`log_summary.warnings`, which is SAS-engine log content: this is
jenner-web speaking about the plan the caller is on. `null` when nothing
was capped. Always serialized (part of the ok:true schema contract);
`None` on a reject.

limits.description:
The execution limits the caller's tier imposes. Present on every run,
capped or not, so an agent can plan before it is truncated rather than
discover the bound afterwards.

listing.description: Printed output — the regulator-style table lives here.

log.description:
The run's SAS log, present only when the caller asked for it via
`include_log` or `log_tail_bytes`. Absent by default, exactly as before.

log_summary.description:
Triage view over the SAS log: the authoritative `level` (reconciled
with the engine exit code), ERROR/WARNING lines, and NOTE count.
The full log is not returned inline BY DEFAULT (every tool return
crosses the caller's context window on each subsequent turn). Ask for it
with `include_log` or `log_tail_bytes` in the same round trip; it is also
persisted in full on the audit and retrievable via
`get_execution_audit`.

ok.description: `true` = the program ran; `false` = the caller's input was rejected.

status.description:
The engine's raw status string (e.g. `"ok"`, `"completed"`) — kept for
provenance, but NOT authoritative: the engine can report `ok` on a
failed step. Trust `log_summary.level` for the real outcome.

truncated.description:
What the caller's own bounds cut short. Empty (and omitted) when the
caller set no bounds, or when nothing exceeded them.

tools.name: get_execution_audit
tools.description: Retrieve a SAS-language execution's auditable artifact by id: the exact program that ran, its content hash, the execution environment, a plain-language description of what the run did, the input context, and the resulting output datasets.

audit_id.description: The `audit_id` of a prior SAS-language execution.

AuditArtifact.description:
One output FILE recorded on the audit — the manifest of what a run
actually produced, so a reviewer can see that a figure or a report existed
even after the gateway's run record has aged out.

No hash at all, where [`AuditDataset::sha256`] at least carries a shape
descriptor. The gateway strips artifact bytes before they reach jenner-web
(`clients::run_api::OutputFile`), so a content hash could only be invented
— and unlike a dataset, an artifact has no name/rows/columns triple to
stand in for one. Size and mime are the whole of what the wire gives us.

AuditDataset.description:
One dataset produced by an execution. `sha256` is a shape descriptor over
`name|rows|columns`, NOT a hash of the dataset bytes: the gateway returns
dataset bytes behind token-scoped URLs rather than inline, so per-dataset
content-addressing is Phase 2. For a genuine output-content hash see
[`ExecutionAudit::output_listing_sha256`].

engine_version.description:
The engine build that produced this result, from
[`crate::clients::run_api::RunOutcome::jenner_version`] — run-api
resolves it by exec'ing the same binary that ran the program, so it
carries the git SHA.

`None` when run-api reported no version, or reported its `"dev"`
placeholder. Never derived from the log: a caller's own output reaches
the log verbatim, and a provenance field must not be forgeable by the
party it describes.

error.description:
Present iff `ok:false`. The rejection reason; deliberately the same
string for every miss, whatever its cause (see 47465).

failure_class.description:
Why the run-api gateway gave no usable result (`gateway_timeout`,
`gateway_unreachable`, `gateway_bad_response`, `gateway_status_<5xx>`).
Such a row keeps no program text and no log, and is the only kind with
this set, so `failure_class IS NOT NULL` is what marks it: `status` is
otherwise the gateway's own string. `None` for every run with an outcome.

ok.description:
`true` = the audit was found and its fields are inlined alongside;
`false` = the request was rejected (see `error`).

organization_id.description: Nullable, best-effort: Phase 1 audit is user-scoped, not org-scoped.

output_artifacts.description:
Files the run wrote (plots, ODS reports, exports). Empty for a run
that produced none, and for any audit written before the manifest
existed — the column defaults to `[]`, so a row from an older writer
reads as "no artifacts" rather than failing to load.

output_listing_sha256.description:
Content hash of the printed output listing (the rendered table the
caller is shown), making the artifact tamper-evident on its output.
Contrast [`AuditDataset::sha256`], which is only a shape descriptor.

request_id.description:
jenner-web's own `x-request-id` (see `mcp::router`), NOT the
gateway's `trace_id` — the gateway never populates that field for
external callers.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Liveness check for the Jenner MCP server.

tools.name: validate_sas_program
tools.description: Validate a SAS-language program (DATA steps, PROC steps, macros, PROC SQL) for parse errors without executing it. Returns ok=true when the program parses cleanly. A program that fails to parse returns ok=false with one or more diagnostics describing each parse issue and no error. A rejected request (for example an empty program) returns ok=false with an error explaining what to fix and no diagnostics.

ToolDiagnostic.description:
One `/v1/validate` diagnostic, reshaped from `clients::run_api::Diagnostic`
for the tool's own output schema (kept separate from the gateway client's
wire type so the two can evolve independently).

diagnostics.description: One entry per parse issue; empty on a clean parse and on a rejection.

error.description:
Present iff the request was REJECTED (empty program, missing scope):
the reason, with no diagnostics. Absent on a parse failure, which
reports itself through `diagnostics` instead.

ok.description:
`true` = the program parsed cleanly; `false` = it failed to parse (see
`diagnostics`) or the request was rejected (see `error`).

jenner-web's own `x-request-id` (see `mcp::router`), NOT the
gateway's `trace_id` — the gateway never populates that field for
external callers.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Liveness check for the Jenner MCP server.

tools.name: validate_sas_program
tools.description: Validate a SAS-language program (DATA steps, PROC steps, macros, PROC SQL) for parse errors without executing it. Returns ok=true when the program parses cleanly. A program that fails to parse returns ok=false with one or more diagnostics describing each parse issue and no error. A rejected request (for example an empty program) returns ok=false with an error explaining what to fix and no diagnostics.

ToolDiagnostic.description:
One `/v1/validate` diagnostic, reshaped from `clients::run_api::Diagnostic`
for the tool's own output schema (kept separate from the gateway client's
wire type so the two can evolve independently).

diagnostics.description: One entry per parse issue; empty on a clean parse and on a rejection.

error.description:
Present iff the request was REJECTED (empty program, missing scope):
the reason, with no diagnostics. Absent on a parse failure, which
reports itself through `diagnostics` instead.

ok.description:
`true` = the program parsed cleanly; `false` = it failed to parse (see
`diagnostics`) or the request was rejected (see `error`).

analysis.token_basis: audit_server countStaticTokens: with-tools minus without-tools input_tokens. No generation.

findings.message: Description does not say when to use this tool.
Description does not say when to use this tool.

controls.name: include_log
controls.description:
Return the run's full SAS log alongside the result.

Omit (the default) and no log is returned, exactly as before; it is
still retrievable afterwards via `get_execution_audit`. Set this to read
the log in the SAME round trip. `log_tail_bytes` implies this.

controls.name: max_listing_bytes
controls.description:
Cap the returned `listing` at this many BYTES, keeping the head.

Omit for the full listing — the default is unchanged and nothing is
trimmed unless you ask. Worth asking: two `PROC PRINT`s over the demo
datasets already return ~27 KB, and an uncapped run over the full 3,200
-row `adlb` is several times a typical client's tool-output budget,
which clients discard silently rather than reporting.

The bound is honoured exactly except that it never splits a multi-byte
character; when that happens the result is a byte or two shorter, and
`truncated` reports what was actually returned.
